title: Hard-earned experience fuels optimism as Grafton football enters Beltner era | Bearcat Sports | wvnews.com
text:
GRAFTON, W.Va. — After undergoing the growing pains of a youth movement, the Grafton football program is poised to reap the rewards of hard-earned experience as it enters a new era under coach Bobby Beltner.
Although the scoreboard hasn’t always rewarded the Bearcats’ efforts, resulting in a 5-35 record over the past four seasons, including a 1-9 finish last fall, many of the players Beltner inherits have seen extensive playing time and experienced firsthand the fine margins that often separate winning from losing.
“There wasn’t much attrition from last year’s team. It’s been a young group for the last couple seasons,” Beltner said. “Luckily, I have the luxury of taking the helm of a team that has a lot of players who have seen live game action, which can only benefit us this year.”
The transition for Beltner and his staff has been eased by their familiarity with much of the roster, having previously coached a majority of the players during his tenure at Taylor County Middle School.
That existing connection has carried into months of offseason work together as the Bearcats prepare for Beltner’s first season in the high school coaching ranks.
“These kids are hungry for success, so it hasn’t been hard convincing them to stay engaged,” Beltner said. “However, it’s just different slipping on the pads for the first time after you’ve been in the weight room and had flex days for months.
“Actually getting to practice full speed and seeing that first game getting closer is a big motivational tool for not just the players, but us coaches too.”
Turning that eagerness into on-the-field results will hinge on Beltner’s staff getting the most out of a proven core of playmakers in Chace Kinsey, Tanner Lipscomb, Jacob Milnarcik, Cash Nestor, John Logan Jones and Randall Grogg.
Kinsey stands at the center of those plans after finding success as a dual-threat signal-caller following his transition from wide receiver to quarterback last season.
He made the most of the position change, rushing for 527 yards and six touchdowns on 116 carries while completing 70 of 142 passes for 677 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions.
The reunion with Beltner has placed the junior dual-threat in a new system that Kinsey believes will make the most of not just his skill set, but the versatile weapons surrounding him.
“Part of our offense feels new, but a lot of it is similar to what I remember. It is pretty simple, but very effective,” Kinsey said. “The scheme will keep opponents guessing and take advantage of matchups.
“I’m excited for the chance to use both my arm and legs to make plays that help our team win.”
“Our offense is going to run through Chace,” Beltner said. “We will go as far as his athleticism, decision-making and leadership takes us.”
Set to join Kinsey in the backfield will be senior running back Cash Nestor, who has played a significant role in Grafton’s ground game since seeing time as a freshman.
Cash Nestor broke out as a sophomore to lead the Bearcats with 818 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 163 attempts while adding five receptions for 113 yards and another score.
Despite battling through injuries last fall, Cash Nestor remained effective, once again pacing Grafton with 772 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 154 carries.
Now healthy, Cash Nestor has his sights set on eclipsing the 1,000-yard mark for the first time in his final season with Grafton.
“We’re very fortunate to have a proven back the caliber of Cash to lean on in the ground game,” Beltner said. “He is a physical runner, but doesn’t sacrifice speed or shiftiness for power, and his hands just add another dimension.”
Out wide, sophomore J.W. Nestor is primed to resume his role as Kinsey’s top target, building on a debut high school season that saw him lead the receiving corps in receptions (22), yards (265) and touchdowns (four).
“Our fans are going to hear J.W.’s name being called a lot this season,” Beltner said. “He is a talent we’re going to game plan touches for within the offense.”
Adding further flexibility to the offense will be seniors Jeremiah Quinn and Keegan Quinn alongside sophomore Jaxson Hussion, giving Beltner three versatile athletes capable of contributing from multiple spots.
“I really like our depth at the skill positions. Look no further than the pair of Jeremiah and Keegan Quinn for the reason why,” Beltner said. “They embody the mindset we want in our team. They’re two of the hardest workers and most fearless players I’ve ever been around.
“Jaxson played quarterback for me his eighth-grade year when we won the championship. He’s too athletic not to have out on the field. He’s going to see time at running back, receiver, corner and special teams.”
Paving the way for that offensive arsenal and setting the tone defensively will be an experienced group in the trenches headlined by seniors Wyatt Cunningham and Abbott Dahl.
“We’re going to be pretty well-rounded up front, and that’s where everything starts for us,” Beltner said. “We have a lot of experience and talent up front, which is something we’re going to utilize to stay fresh.”
Stewarding the defense behind their deep line will be senior linebacker Tanner Lipscomb, who returns after leading Grafton with 51 tackles and adding an interception last season.
“I feel it’s my job to stay aggressive while playing smart,” Lipscomb said. “That boils down to understanding what’s going on around you, reading your keys and knowing what everyone on the defense is doing, which are all things I’ve gotten better at each year. Now I can’t wait to lead the defense back on the field this year.”
Beltner is equally optimistic about the back end of the defense.
“Our cornerbacks and safeties are going to be really good,” Beltner said. “We have a lot of athleticism back there and guys we trust to make plays when the opportunity comes.”
Rounding out Grafton’s outlook across all three phases, the capable sophomore duo of Colin McCarthy and Dylan Stead will handle kicking and punting duties.
With the pieces in place, the next step is putting everything together against a formidable slate.
“We’ve got a 10-game schedule, and eight teams on our schedule were in the playoffs last year, so it’s not going to be easy,” Beltner said. “We know that, and the kids know that.”
Still, Beltner believes the best way to capitalize on that experience is to keep the focus simple.
“We want to be better today than we were yesterday, and we just want to keep working,” Beltner said. “If we do those two things, the wins and losses will take care of themselves eventually.”
That pursuit begins when Grafton travels to Philippi to face rival Philip Barbour on Friday, Aug. 28, at 7 p.m.
